samples.summary: Clamping `t` to read-time `Date.now()` does not achieve the stated invariant — a future timestamp still outranks every genuine edit, and a clock-ahead peer permanently owns its line
samples.evidence: `sanitizeWrittenAt` returns `Math.min(value, now)` where `now = Date.now()` is taken at read time (line 161). The documented goal (lines 56-61, and docs/design/notes/notes.md:582-584) is that "clamping to `now` reduces a forged timestamp to a tie, which document order then breaks". It does not: every genuine run's `at` is the wall-clock instant it was written, i.e. strictly LESS than the reader's `now` (except in the same millisecond). So a run claiming `t = 4e15` is re-clamped to the current instant on every read and therefore compares as strictly newest against every earlier genuine run; `authorOfRange` (packages/notes/src/view/blame-gutter.ts:48) picks it, exactly the outcome the clamp claims to prevent — and it keeps winning after every subsequent genuine edit too, because the next read clamps it to a newer `now` again. The same logic misattributes benign cases: a peer whose clock is minutes ahead writes a future `t`, and its run then outranks later edits by other users on the same line until real time catches up. The new test only asserts `at <= Date.now()`, so it passes without the invariant holding. A clamp that reads as "unknown" (0) for anything in the future, or one anchored to a per-run first-observed timestamp, would actually enforce the documented behavior.

samples.summary: `slice(0, 64)` cuts by UTF-16 code unit and can split a surrogate pair, leaving a lone surrogate in the label
samples.evidence: `value.replace(...).slice(0, MAX_AUTHOR_LENGTH)` truncates at code-unit 64. If code units 63/64 are a surrogate pair (any astral character — emoji, many CJK ext, Deseret…), the result ends in an unpaired high surrogate, which renders as U+FFFD in the gutter and in the new hover title, and is also written into the CRDT by `editText` (line 145) so the corruption is persisted, not just displayed. Truncating on a code-point (or grapheme) boundary avoids this.

samples.summary: Stripping all of `\p{Cf}` removes ZWJ/ZWNJ, mangling legitimate names and emoji, and the mangled form is persisted on write
samples.evidence: `\p{Cf}` includes U+200D ZERO WIDTH JOINER and U+200C ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER. These are required for correct rendering of Persian/Arabic and Indic names, and for ZWJ emoji sequences: a presence name like "👨‍👩‍👧" becomes three separate glyphs and a Persian name loses its non-joiner. Because `editText` (line 145) sanitizes on the way in as well, the mangled name is what goes into the CRDT permanently, not just what is shown. Only the bidi-override/isolate set (U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069) and true zero-width invisibles need removing here.

samples.summary: Sanitizer misses the line/paragraph separators and other invisibles it claims to remove
samples.evidence: The doc comment (lines 44-48) and docs/design/notes/notes.md:584-587 claim the name cannot "break the gutter out of its single line". U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR and U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR are general category Zl/Zp, so they survive `[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}]`, as do invisible letter-category characters (e.g. U+3164 HANGUL FILLER) and unbounded stacking combining marks (\p{Mn}) that can overflow a 6.5em column vertically. Impact is display-only (white-space: nowrap likely folds the separators), hence low confidence and minor, but the stated contract is broader than the regex.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. `sanitizeWrittenAt` (yorkie-note-store.ts:63-68) returns `Math.min(value, now)` with `now = Date.now()` read at walk time (line 161, applied line 177). The documented invariant at lines 55-61 and docs/design/notes/notes.md:582-584 claims clamping turns a future timestamp into a "tie that document order breaks" — it does not. Genuine runs carry the wall-clock instant they were written (editText line 146), which is strictly less than a later reader's `now`, so a run claiming `t = 4e15` is re-clamped to the current instant on every read and compares strictly greatest. `authorOfRange` (packages/notes/src/view/blame-gutter.ts:48, `span.at >= best.at`) therefore picks it, and keeps picking it after each subsequent genuine edit because the next read clamps it forward again. This also fires benignly: a peer with a clock minutes ahead writes a future `t` and its run outranks genuinely later edits by other users on the same line, so computeBlameLabels (blame-gutter.ts:71) renders the wrong author — a wrong-comparison logic bug in the correctness lane, not merely a security concern. No upper-bound guard exists anywhere: getAuthorSpans is the only producer of `at` and authorOfRange the only consumer. The new test (yorkie-note-store.test.ts:233-245) asserts only `at <= Date.now()`, which the clamp satisfies while the forged run still wins the label, so it passes without the invariant holding.
